action: Development teams, especially in crypto: review .claude/settings.json files in repositories for commands you did not add, treat changes to them like code changes, audit GitHub access tokens with Copilot-style names, and warn staff not to run fix scripts from meeting pages.
exec: Developer tool configuration files are being abused for persistent access at crypto firms; treat them as code.
plain: Google says suspected North Korean hackers tricked staff at cryptocurrency firms into running harmful commands, then altered a settings file in code projects so that opening an AI coding tool installed a hidden backdoor.

key_findings: Google describes recent intrusions against cryptocurrency organisations in North America and Europe by a suspected MIDNIGHT NEPTUNE cluster it links to North Korea.
Fake recruiter profiles with AI-generated images steered targets to bogus meeting platforms, where ClickFix prompts had them run fix scripts that were likely LLM-written.
Inside victim networks the actor edited .claude/settings.json in internal code repositories so that starting Claude Code downloaded the SOMBERMEME backdoor.
The actor created GitHub personal access tokens named after Microsoft Copilot to disguise lateral movement.
Google frames this as abuse of native AI agent execution hooks and an internal supply chain vector; the post gives no indicator list.
recommendations: The post gives no step-by-step guidance for this activity; it points to Mandiant's hardening guide for machine-speed, LLM-enabled tooling.
Verify LLM-generated proof-of-concept exploits before relying on them, since many published ones do not work.

summary: Google's November 16 AI Threat Tracker says a suspected North Korean cluster, MIDNIGHT NEPTUNE, used fake recruiter profiles and ClickFix lures against cryptocurrency organisations in North America and Europe. After getting in, it edited .claude/settings.json files in internal code repositories so that starting Claude Code downloaded the SOMBERMEME backdoor. The post does not say whether this is a product flaw and lists no indicators.
title: Google: North Korean actor backdoors crypto developers through Claude Code settings files

validation.note: Reviewed against the original Google Threat Intelligence Group document.
